html:
SMTO-SKL-0017 — SMTO couldn't find that calendar event

GUID: 9d85031a-7e0e-5f7c-a82e-0e6291ba610d
Slug: google-calendar-event-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • The event SMTO tried to use isn't in that calendar any more, or this account can't see it. It may have been deleted or cancelled. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Google Calendar in your browser and look for the event on its date. Check whether it was deleted, or cancelled by its organizer. A deleted or cancelled event can't be edited, so SMTO stopped.
  2. If the event is still there, ask SMTO to search your calendar for it again on that date, then repeat your request. A fresh search gives SMTO the event's current details, in case it moved or changed calendars.
  3. If the event is gone and you still need it, ask SMTO to create a new event with the details you want. SMTO won't recreate a missing event or pick a similar one on its own.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the event on the date you expect and your change appears in Google Calendar.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to change a different event that only has the same title; it could be the wrong meeting.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google returned 404 or 410 for an event-scoped Calendar request, or the pre-write read of the exact event_id reported status cancelled.

What this means

  • Google returns event-scoped HTTP 404/410, or the pre-write event read reports status cancelled. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns event-scoped HTTP 404/410, or the pre-write event read reports status cancelled.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact calendar/event IDs and the pre-write event status.

How to fix it

  • Read the exact calendar_id and event_id under the intended account_ref with google_calendar.event or a bounded google_calendar.events search; the event may be deleted, cancelled or no longer visible. Do not create a substitute event or pick another event by title.
  • Inspect the exact calendar_id and event_id under the intended account. The event may have been deleted, cancelled or become inaccessible.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact calendar_id and event_id under the intended account. The event may have been deleted, cancelled or become inaccessible.

How to verify the fix

  • Recovery uses the intended current event without creating a substitute by title.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
